question: Find the value of $k$ for which the function $$f(x)=\begin{cases}kx+1, & x\leq 2\\3x-1, & x>2\end{cases}$$ is continuous at $x=2$. Justify your answer.
explanation:
Continuity condition at $x=2$
For continuity, the left-hand limit, right-hand limit and $f(2)$ must be equal.
Left-hand limit and function value
$$\lim_{x\to 2^-}f(x)=2k+1$$
Since $x\leq 2$ in the first branch, $$f(2)=2k+1$$
Right-hand limit
$$\lim_{x\to 2^+}f(x)=3(2)-1=5$$
Equating the limits
$$2k+1=5$$
$$k=2$$
Hence, the function is continuous at $x=2$ when $k=2$.
